title: Собрать канонические воспроизводимые private RC subjects и receipt schema
summary: Построить три repository-owned normalized package subjects и доказать byte-for-byte воспроизводимость в независимых clean directories.
why: Native package preview/archive commands помогают проверить contents, но не обещают одинаковые archive bytes; provenance обязана ссылаться на заранее определённый exact subject. `RAG:✅` reproducible-build and packaging evidence в `@plan/knowledge/research-P9-design-rag.json`.

include: Canonical private RC identity; PHP, Dart core и Dart MCP companion subjects; P7 allowlist/content-manifest consumption; normalized path order, metadata, modes, ownership, timestamps and gzip header; `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from source commit; canonical content manifest; SHA-256 checksum set; two independent clean builds; schema-versioned per-subject and aggregate receipt contract; explicit private paired-artifact status for MCP path dependency.
exclude: Composer/pub registry-compatible byte identity claim; public version/tag; registry upload; SBOM/provenance generation; GitHub workflow transport; changing package contents or dependencies; treating a source checkout tarball as the package.

rules: The canonical subject format is repository-owned POSIX tar plus deterministic gzip: bytewise sorted normalized relative paths, rejected traversal/symlink escape/special files, fixed owner/group IDs and names, fixed modes by declared executable policy, fixed mtime from source commit, deleted variable PAX atime/ctime headers and gzip name/time suppression. Build roots and output paths never enter contents. Two builders use separate clean copies and no shared package cache for assembly. Native Composer/Dart previews and P7 manifests are independent content oracles, not canonical byte producers. RC identity is source/contract based and cannot imply a public semver/tag. MCP companion stays `private-paired`/`public-release-blocked` while it has a path dependency.
guidance: Separate content selection from archive serialization and checksum receipt writing. Refuse dirty/untracked product inputs unless explicitly represented in a test fixture. Stream hashes and archive entries; record source/tree/manifest/tool-lock/algorithm digests. Compare content manifests before archive digests so a mismatch is diagnosable. Keep SBOM/provenance outside subject bytes to avoid self-reference.
deliverables: Normative private-RC contract/schema, deterministic builder, three exact candidate subjects with SHA-256/content manifests and independent reproducibility receipt.

sections.title: Validation
